clue.text: Patron from the nearby army depot?

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who shops at the same place habitually
second meaning, whimsical: a shopper who is a regular, a full-time professional soldier from the barracks

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper notes a customer who comes in from the local barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: Regular soldiers are full-time professionals, as opposed to reservists; the question mark flags the pun on the word for a frequent shopper.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron of a shop who visits habitually is known by this two-word phrase, the first word punning on professional soldiers.

clue.text: One training fruit producers?

blocks.note: surface reading: a coach or teacher, someone who trains people
setter's reading: the things trained are fruit trees, tied flat against a wall or frame as they grow

explanation.surface: A coach working with growers who produce fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Training' looks like coaching people, but gardeners train trees by guiding their branches along a lattice.
explanation.definitionFit: This lattice or trellis framework guides the branches of fruit trees flat against a wall, so it literally trains them.

clue.text: Crossword compiler raised boy's honour

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting a word up means reading it from bottom to top

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as me
a boy is a lad; the possessive just joins the surface

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter's son, raised by him, receives an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossword compiler' is the setter speaking of themself, giving ME; the lad is then read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A decoration awarded for bravery or achievement is an honour bestowed on the recipient.

clue.text: Can re-order new tyres on-line

something new is made fresh, so these letters take a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopper orders replacement tyres over the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on-line' looks like internet shopping, but it splits: 'on' joins, and 'line' is the definition. Two separate small shuffles sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Your line is your family descent or lineage, the series of forebears from whom you come.

clue.text: Are including a bull at both ends, fit for ploughing

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within, so one word wraps the others
only the extremities of the word are wanted, its first and last letters

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the first and last letters of bull

explanation.surface: A farmer weighs up whether a field with a bull at either end can be ploughed.
explanation.definitionFit: Land described this way is suitable for growing crops, which means it can be tilled and cultivated.

clue.text: Dictionary he's taken into the "Bull"

indicators.note: something taken into a place ends up inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
Taurus is the bull of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Someone has been carried into a pub called the Bull with a reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks suggest a pub name, but the Bull is the zodiac sign Taurus.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of synonyms is a kind of dictionary of words grouped by meaning, a word-finder for writers.

clue.text: Supply a slide

blocks.note: taken as written
a slide for a projector or microscope is a mount, the frame holding the image or specimen

explanation.surface: An instruction to provide a playground slide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' reads as a verb, but it is the noun: a supply of something is a quantity of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A supply of goods means a quantity or stock of them, the total sum available.

clue.text: Finds Des in rally, travelling around Tonga

indicators.note: letters that travel around move about from place to place and land in new positions

blocks.note: taken as written, all fifteen letters

explanation.surface: A man called Des is spotted at a motor rally touring the Pacific kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: The rally sounds like a car event, but it is part of the material to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Cook gave this nickname to the Pacific archipelago of Tonga after the warm welcome he received there.

clue.text: Oriental ruler chasing unusual sea bird

indicators.note: an unusual form is not the normal one, so these letters appear out of their usual order
a thing chasing another comes after it, so this piece is placed at the end

blocks.note: taken as written
a tern is a seabird
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An Eastern monarch pursues a rare seabird.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the standard crossword ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the East or the Orient is described as such; both words name someone from Asian lands.

clue.text: Domestic right for a poet

blocks.note: home as an adjective means domestic, as in home affairs
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone argues a poet has a right to a home.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek author of the Iliad and Odyssey is the most famous epic poet of all.

clue.text: Unenlightened article on battle in a foreign one

something in another thing is placed inside it, enclosed by its letters

blocks.note: the indefinite article

explanation.walkthrough: 'a foreign one' is French une, which wraps the article and the battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unaware lacks knowledge or information, which is exactly what being unenlightened means.

clue.text: Drawbridge made of copper in a Swiss city

indicators.note: something in a place sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
Basle is the older English spelling of Basel

explanation.surface: A Swiss bridge constructed out of copper.
explanation.walkthrough: Basle is the traditional English spelling of the Swiss city Basel.
explanation.definitionFit: This counterweighted type of bridge, like Tower Bridge in London, has spans that swing upward like a drawbridge.

clue.text: Very keen now about six

indicators.note: about here means around, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era, the years of now
six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone is eager to talk about six right now.
explanation.walkthrough: AD for 'now' is a crossword convention: we live in the AD era.
explanation.definitionFit: An avid fan is eager and enthusiastic, wanting something intensely, the same as being very keen.

clue.text: Ted ate tuna salad, becoming thin

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dieter called Ted eats a tuna salad and slims down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salad' looks like part of the meal, but it signals the mix-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something attenuated has been drawn out and made slender or weakened, so it is thin.

clue.text: School functioned, though only taking up a small space

blocks.note: comp is short for comprehensive, a British state secondary school
to act is to function or operate

explanation.surface: A school is working well despite its cramped premises.
explanation.walkthrough: A comp, short for comprehensive, is a British state secondary school that takes pupils of all abilities.
explanation.definitionFit: Material that has been compacted is pressed tightly together, so it occupies little room.

clue.text: Offhand, despicable people love going by railway

love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Nasty people are dismissive of love affairs conducted by train.
explanation.definitionFit: A cursory glance is hasty and superficial, done without care, much like an offhand remark.

clue.text: Turn coy, ending up in a state?

indicators.note: the words finish up as something different, so their letters are rearranged into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grows shy and ends up flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' is a common phrase for being agitated, which hides the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation or sovereign land, with its own government, is both a country and a state.

clue.text: Birds on a jail sign

blocks.note: can is slang for prison
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Birds perched on a prison noticeboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign' looks like a notice on the jail wall, but it is a sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: These small yellow songbirds, kept as pets and once in mines, are a family of finches.

clue.text: Decline to take unmarried twin to fair

indicators.note: unmarried means no longer joined, so the word is cut and loses its end

blocks.note: taken as written
fair hair or skin is light in colour

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to bring an unwed twin along to the funfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like a verb meaning refuse, but it is the noun for a waning period; the twin loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The twilight of a career or life is its final waning period, a time of gradual decline.

clue.text: Hastily running pipe round mobile home

a camper is a camper van, a home on wheels

explanation.surface: Someone rushes past with a pipe around a caravan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pipe' looks like a tube, but it is the verb: to sing shrilly.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to run quickly and lightly, like a small animal dashing about in a hurry.

clue.text: Demonstrate some ideas Watt established

indicators.note: only some of the following text is used, a run of letters inside it

blocks.note: surface padding: only the text after it holds the letters
the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Showing some of the ideas that the engineer James Watt established.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest to something is to bear witness and give proof of it, which is to show or prove it.

clue.text: Widow's souvenir tin-opener

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, the one that begins it

blocks.note: a relic is a keepsake or memento of the past
the first letter of tin

explanation.surface: A widow keeps a tin-opener as a memento.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tin-opener' looks like a kitchen tool, but it splits into tin and its opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Relict is an archaic or legal word for a widow, the woman left behind after her husband dies.

clue.text: Excellent woman objects

blocks.note: A1 means first-class; the digit 1 is read as the letter I
Ms is a title for a woman

explanation.surface: A fine woman raises objections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'objects' looks like a verb, but it is the plural noun for goals.
explanation.definitionFit: Your aims are your goals or purposes, and the objects of an effort are its intended targets.

clue.text: Way to help to become sober

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
aid means help

explanation.surface: A method for helping someone sober up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sober' looks like not drunk, but here it means serious and restrained.
explanation.definitionFit: A staid person is sedate, serious and unadventurous, which matches sober in its sense of grave.

clue.text: Work on Act I upset student of vision

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a work
taken as written
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.walkthrough: 'student of vision' reads like an eye scientist, but the definition is just 'of vision'.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical describes anything relating to sight or the eye, so it means pertaining to vision.

clue.text: Wine found amongst the clarets in any cellar

clue.text: Follow to make certain ringleader's gone

clue.text: Nursed by a famous female singer I dropped off

taken as written
